Any word that describes or qualifies a noun is an adjective, and one placed after a linking verb in this way is a predicative adjective. Test the other labels against the word. It cannot be a noun, because it names no person or thing and could not take an article before it. It cannot be an adverb, because it qualifies the noun 'conclusions' rather than a verb, and note that it is itself qualified by 'highly', which is an adverb doing its normal job of modifying an adjective. It cannot be a gerund, because a gerund is a verb form ending in -ing that is used as a noun, and this word is neither an -ing form nor a noun. So the underlined word is an adjective. Matches option B.

It is not a noun, since it names nothing and could not take an article. It is not an adverb: it qualifies a noun rather than a verb, and it is itself qualified by the adverb 'highly', which is what adverbs do to adjectives. It is not a gerund, since a gerund is an -ing verb form used as a noun and 'questionable' is neither.]

subject: Polity

stem: If the Prime Minister is taken from the Rajya Sabha
optA: he must get elected to the Lok Sabha within six months.
optB: he can make policy Statements only in the Rajya Sabha.
optC: he cannot take part in the voting when a vote of no confidence is under consideration.
optD: he cannot take part in the budget deliberations in Lok Sabha.
solution: The Rajya Sabha cannot remove the council of ministers by passing a no-confidence motion. • This is because the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible only to the Lok Sabha. • But the Rajya Sabha can discuss and criticise the policies and activities of the government. Hence, if the Prime Minister is a member of the Rajya Sabha, he will not be able to vote in favour in the event of the no-confidence motion. Being a Prime Minister, he can make statements in both Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha. The Constitution does not contain any specific procedure for the selection and appointment of the Prime Minister. Article 75 simply states that the Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President. Constitutionally, the Prime Minister may be a member of either of the two Houses of Parliament. For example, three Prime Ministers, Indira Gandhi (1966), Deve Gowda (1996) and Manmohan Singh (2004), were members of the Rajya Sabha. The term of the Prime Minister is not fixed, and he holds office during the pleasure of the President. The Prime Minister is the leader of the Lower House.

stem: The two Houses of Parliament enjoy co-equal power in all spheres except I. financial matters II. responsibility of the Council of Ministers III. amendment procedure IV. election of President
solution: The two Houses of Parliament, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, have equal powers in many areas, but their roles diverge in specific matters: Financial Matters: The Lok Sabha holds more power in financial matters. Money bills must originate in the Lok Sabha, and while the Rajya Sabha can suggest amendments, it cannot alter or reject them. Responsibility of the Council of Ministers: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, meaning it is answerable to it. The Rajya Sabha cannot remove the government or pass a vote of no confidence. However, in areas like the constitutional amendment procedure and the election of the President, both Houses have co-equal authority.

stem: At a joint sitting of Parliament a bill has to be passed
optA: by a simple majority of the total number of members of both Houses.

optC: by a simple majority of the total number of members of both Houses present and voting.
optD: by a two-thirds majority of the total number of members of both Houses present and voting.
solution: In a joint sitting of Parliament, a bill is passed by a simple majority of the members who are present and voting. This means the majority is determined by the votes of those present, not by the total number of members from both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.This process occurs when the two Houses of Parliament disagree on a bill, and the President of India calls for a joint sitting to resolve the deadlock. The decision is taken by the majority of members present and voting, and there is no requirement for a two-thirds majority in this case.

solution: The Committee on Public Assurances is tasked with reviewing whether the promises or commitments made by ministers during parliamentary debates have been fulfilled. Consider the following statements with respect to Khilafat Movement.
1. Maulana Abul Kalam Azad launched this Anti- British revolutionary movement.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution: The All India Khilafat Committee was created in 1919 at Lucknow. It was founded by Ali Brothers (Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali), Ahmed Ansari, Hasrat Mohanani, Abul Kalam Azad, Hakim Ajmal Khan and others. The committee had two demands: one is that Khalifa must control Muslim sacred places, and the other is to retain sufficient territories under Khalifa. Abul Kalam Azad presided over the Congress special session in Delhi in 1923. He became the youngest President of the Indian National Congress and was re-elected as President during the Ramgarh session in 1940. In addition to his political achievements, he served as the head of the Jamat-ul-Ulema in 1924 and presided over the Nationalist Muslim Conference five years later in the same capacity.

2. Mahatma Gandhi was invited by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel to visit Champaran district.
solution: Champaran Satyagraha (1917): Gandhi’s first great experiment in satyagraha came in 1917 in Champaran, a district of Bihar. The peasantry on the indigo plantations in the district was excessively oppressed by the European planters. They were compelled to grow indigo on at least 3120th of their land. And so sell it at prices fixed by the planters. This system was popularly known as ‘Tin-Kathia system’. Accompanied by Babu Rajendra Prasad, Mazhar- Lil-Huq, J.B. Kriplani, Narhari Parekh and Mahadev Desai, Gandhiji reached Champaran in 1917. Gandhiji won his first battle of civil disobedience in India. He was invited by Raj Kumar Shukla, a peasant among the champaran people.

solution: The Ancient Iron Age in India is associated with Painted Grey Ware (PGW) pottery: PGW is a pottery tradition that is grey in colour with black geometric designs. The PGW culture lasted from roughly 1100 to 800 BCE and is associated with the Kuru-Panchala kingdom, the first large state in South Asia. The PGW culture succeeded the Black and Red Ware Culture in the eastern Ganga Valley and Central India. The PGW culture is followed by the Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW) culture, which is associated with the Mahajanapada and Mauryan periods. The earliest evidence for smelted iron in India dates to 1300 to 1000 BCE. The central Indian region seems to be the earliest iron-using centre.

solution: Both statements are correct about the Alipore Bomb Conspiracy: • Douglas Kingsford was the target of the bomb thrown at Muzaffarpur. • Prafulla Chaki and Khudiram Bose were the main culprits of the case. The Alipore Bomb Conspiracy, also known as the Maniktala bomb conspiracy, was a revolutionary act against British rule in India in 1908: • The target was Douglas Kingsford, an unpopular British Chief Magistrate in Muzaffarpur, Bihar. • Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki threw a bomb at a carriage they believed was carrying Kingsford. • The bomb killed two British women instead of Kingsford due to mistaken identity. • The Alipore conspiracy trial was held between May 1908 and May 1909 in Calcutta. • Other defendants in the case included Aurobindo Ghosh, his brother Barin Ghosh, Satyendranath Bose, and Kanailal Dutt. • Prafulla Chaki committed suicide, and Khudiram Bose was hanged at the age of 18.

stem: In which session of Congress was the demand of “Purna Swaraj” accepted as its aim?
solution: Lahore Congress Session: The Indian National Congress (INC), on 19 December 1929, passed the historic “Purna Swaraj resolution” at its Lahore session. A public announcement was made on 26 January 1930, a day which the Congress Party selected for the Indians to celebrate as “Independence Day”. 26th January 1930 was declared as Purna Swaraj Diwas. Pandit Jawahar Lal Nehru presided over the Lahore Congress session. Jawaharlal Nehru hoisted the tricolour flag of India.

subject: History
stem: Which religious reformer of Western India was known as ‘Lokhitwadi’?
solution: Gopal Hari Deshmukh, also known as Lokhitwadi, was a social reformer who started the newspaper Lokhitwadi to address social issues. He advocated for reforms like education, widow remarriage and women’s rights, emphasising the need to reshape society based on rational and modern values. Deshmukh famously stated, “If religion does not sanction social reform, then change the religion”. He wrote books like Panipat War, Kalyog, Jatibhed and Lankecha Itihas and translated English works into Marathi. He was honoured with the title Rao Bahadur.

Which of the following statements is/are correct about Indian Universities Act?
1. Indian Universities Act was passed in 1904 during the time of Lord Curzon.
2. It was formed on the recommendations of Rayleigh commission. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution: Lord Curzon, the British Viceroy of India, passed the Indian Universities Act in 1904. The act was based on the recommendations of the University Commission, which was established in 1902 and headed by Sir Thomas Raleigh. solution: After the 1935 elections, the Indian National Congress (INC) formed ministries in most provinces, reflecting its strong political presence. However, Bengal and Punjab were exceptions. In Bengal, the Muslim League formed the government, and in Punjab, the Unionist Party took power. These provinces did not have Congress ministries, primarily due to political dynamics and communal factors that influenced the outcomes of the elections.

Persuade the British government and British public opinion to introduce reforms in India on the lines laid out by the nationalists.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: Peechi wildlife sanctuary, recently seen in the news, is located in which state?
solution: A female elephant recently died from electrocution near a tribal colony close to Peechi Wildlife Sanctuary in Kerala’s Thrissur district. Peechi-Vazhani Wildlife Sanctuary, established in 1958, covers 125 sq. km in Thrissur. It is located in the catchment area of Peechi and Vazhani Dams and is part of the Palapilli-Nelliampathy forests. The terrain varies in altitude from 100 to 914 m, with Ponmudi as the highest peak. The sanctuary has tropical forests, 50+ orchid species, rare medicinal plants and valuable trees like teak.

stem: What is the primary reservoir of the Rocahepevirus ratti strain of hepatitis E virus (HEV), recently in news?
solution: Recent studies indicate that the Rocahepevirus ratti strain, commonly known as “rat HEV”, primarily resides in rats and has been found to infect humans. Since its first human case in 2018, at least 20 cases have been reported, often linked to the consumption of raw pork. Researchers discovered that rat HEV could infect pigs and spread among them, highlighting concerns for the pork industry as a potential pathway for human infection. Hepatitis E remains a significant global health issue, particularly in developing regions.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: Recently, which state secured the top rank in the Urban Governance Index (UGI)?
solution: Kerala has achieved the top rank in the Urban Governance Index (UGI), a study by the Praja Foundation assessing cities in India. Scoring 59.31 out of 100, it excelled in fiscal empowerment and local governance. The state’s commitment to decentralised planning has been acknowledged, despite challenges in city administration empowerment. Odisha followed in second place with a score of 55.10, highlighting the competitive nature of urban governance across India.

solution: The headquarters of the Theosophical Society (TS) is located in Adyar, Chennai, India. The Theosophical Society was founded in New York in 1875 by Madame H. P. Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott. The society’s headquarters were moved to Adyar in 1882. The Theosophical Society’s philosophy is a combination of mysticism, spiritualism, metaphysics, and Buddhist and Hindu thought. The society’s goals include studying and explaining occultism and the Cabala and promoting unity. The US National Section of the Theosophical Society is located in Wheaton, Illinois.

stem: What is the name of mission recently launched by Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways to promote cruise tourism in India?
solution: Union Minister Sarabanand Sonowal launched the Cruise Bharat Mission on 30 September 2024 in Mumbai, Maharashtra. The mission aims to make India a global hub for cruise tourism and a top cruise destination. The Union Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways will implement the mission with support from various regulatory agencies. A special purpose vehicle (SPV) for cruise development will be set up under the Indian Ports Association. The mission will run from 1 October 2024 to 31 March 2029 in three phases.

solution: President Droupadi Murmu laid the foundation stone of state-owned energy firm SJVN’s 1,000 MW Bikaner Solar Power Project in Jaipur, Rajasthan. This project is being implemented by SJVN Limited through its wholly owned subsidiary SJVN Green Energy Limited (SGEL). Bikaner is one of the highest solar yield areas of the country. The project is scheduled to be commissioned by March 2024. SJVN is a leading power CPSE under the Ministry of Power.

solution: NASA cancelled the Volatiles Investigating Polar Exploration Rover (VIPER) mission due to delays and high costs. VIPER was fully assembled and partially tested before cancellation. stem: An electric wire of resistance 50 W is cut into five equal wire. This wire are connected in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance of this combination ?

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which one of the following is a chemical change?
solution: Milk turning sour is a chemical change, while dissolving sugar in water, melting of ice and crystallisation are physical changes. Milk turning sour: In this chemical change, the lactic acid bacteria in milk metabolise the lactose sugar, forming lactic acid. This process is irreversible and creates a new substance with different properties than milk. Dissolving sugar in water: This is a physical change because no reaction takes place between the sugar and water, and no new substances are formed. Melting of ice: This is a physical change because the solid ice is converted into liquid water without any change in the chemical composition of the substance. Crystallisation: This is a physical change because it is a process to change liquids and make them solids.

solution: The valency of the carbonate anion is –2, which means it can combine with cations that have a valency of +2. To balance the charges, we need two ammonium ions (+1) to combine with one carbonate anion (-2). Therefore, the molecular formula of ammonium carbonate is (NH4)2CO3.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which one of the following is a covalent compound?
solution: Silicon oxide (SiO2) is a covalent compound, meaning its atoms are bonded through the sharing of electrons. In SiO2, each silicon atom forms covalent bonds with oxygen atoms, creating a stable structure. In contrast, compounds like calcium oxide (CaO), sodium oxide (Na2O) and zinc sulphide (ZnS) are ionic in nature. In these compounds, electrons are transferred from one atom to another, forming positively and negatively charged ions that are held together by electrostatic forces.

subject: Physics
chapter: Fluid Mechanics and Properties of Matter
stem: A liquid rises to a certain length in a capillary tube. The tube is inclined to an angle of 45oC. The length of the liquid column will
solution: When a capillary tube is inclined at an angle, the vertical height of the liquid column stays the same. This is because the vertical height is determined by the balance of cohesive and adhesive forces, as well as the liquid’s weight. However, the length of the liquid column along the inclined tube increases. This happens because the liquid extends along the longer path of the tilted tube while maintaining the same vertical height. The relationship between the length of the liquid column (L) and the vertical height (h) is given by: h = L sin(q) Where: h: The vertical height (remains constant), L: The length of the liquid column along the tube, q: The angle of inclination of the tube. When the tube is inclined (e.g., to 45°), the sine of the angle (sin(q)) decreases. To keep h constant, the length of the liquid column (L) must increase.
reviewNote: CROSS-PAPER KEY CONFLICT, resolved in THIS paper's favour. m4g Q20 is the same question with an identical option set and keys (c) 'Remain unchanged'; m8 keys (a) 'Increase'. Derivation: capillary rise fixes the VERTICAL height h = 2T cos(theta) / (r rho g), which is independent of the tube's tilt. The stem asks for the LENGTH of the liquid column, measured along the tube, and L = h / cos(45) (angle taken from the vertical) = h / sin(45) (angle taken from the horizontal) = h x sqrt(2) ~ 1.41h either way. So the LENGTH increases while the HEIGHT is unchanged: (a) is correct, and m4g's key (c) answers the question the stem does not ask. m8's printed solution derives this correctly (h = L sin(theta) with h constant, so L must rise); m4g prints no solution at all. m8's key stands; m4g Q20's key is the wrong one.

subject: Physics
stem: A body is at rest on the surface of the earth. Which one among the following statements is correct regarding this?
optA: No force is acting on the body.
optB: Only weight of the body acts on it.
optC: Net downward force is equal to the net upward force.
solution: The body is in equilibrium, meaning the net force acting on it is zero. The net downward force is equal to the net upward force, which is the normal force. Gravity from the Earth is one of the most important forces acting on the object. The frictional force that acts on a body when it is at rest relative to the surface is known as static friction.

subject: Physics
stem: A pendulum beats, faster than a standard pendulum. In order to bring it to the standard beat, the length of the pendulum is to be
optC: reduced and the mass of the bob increased.
optD: reduced and also the mass of the bob reduced.
solution: When a pendulum beats faster than the standard beat, it means that it takes less time for each swing. This can happen when the length of the pendulum is shorter than the standard length. The time it takes for a pendulum to complete one full swing is directly proportional to the length of the pendulum. So, if we want to bring a faster-beating pendulum to the standard beat, we need to increase the length of the pendulum. By increasing the length, the time taken for each swing will increase, and the pendulum will beat at the standard rate. It is important to note that changing the mass of the bob (the weight at the end of the pendulum) or reducing both the length and mass (option 3 or 4) will not bring the pendulum to the standard beat.
reviewNote: Rule 5 (minor): the solution says the period is "directly proportional to the length" when T varies as sqrt(L); the conclusion (increase the length) is unaffected.

subject: Physics
stem: A body initially at rest is acted upon by a constant force. The rate of change of its kinetic energy varies
optA: linearly with square root of time.
solution: The rate of change of kinetic energy is equivalent to the power, which is the product of force and velocity. Since the force is constant, both power and the rate of change of kinetic energy increase linearly with velocity. Under constant acceleration, which occurs when a constant force is applied, the velocity increases linearly with time. As the rate of change of kinetic energy is directly proportional to velocity, it also increases linearly with time.

stem: Metal pipes used to carry water sometimes burst in the winter. This is because

solution: When water freezes, it expands and turns into ice, which takes up more space than the liquid water. This expansion increases the pressure inside the pipe, which can cause it to rupture if the pressure becomes too high. Chemical anomaly: Water’s expansion when it freezes is a chemical anomaly, as most chemical compounds contract when they solidify.

subject: Physics
stem: In a pressure cooker, cooking is faster because the increases in vapour pressure
solution: In a pressure cooker, the cooking process is faster because the increase in vapour pressure causes the boiling point of water to rise. This allows the temperature inside the cooker to exceed the normal boiling point of water (100°C or 212°F), enabling food to cook at a higher temperature. As a result, cooking times are reduced since the food is exposed to more heat.
reviewNote: [RESOLVED — a second, independent blind derivation reached the printed key (D) without seeing it or the earlier objection, so the key stands. Basis: A liquid boils when its saturated vapour pressure equals the pressure on its surface. The sealed cooker traps the steam, so the pressure above the water rises well above atmospheric, and the water must be heated further before its vapour pressure can match that raised value; boiling therefore begins above one hundred degrees celsius and the food is held at that higher temperature, which is why it cooks faster. Specific heat is a property of the substance and is not altered by the cooker, so the two options about it are irrelevant, and the boiling point rises rather than falls. Polarity note: nothing in the stem is negated, so the direction asked for is the direction of the change.]

stem: ‘Pitch’ is a characteristic of sound that depends upon its
solution: Pitch is a measure of how high or low a sound is perceived. The frequency of a sound wave determines its pitch, with higher frequency sounds having a higher pitch and lower frequency sounds having a lower pitch. For example, a bird’s chirp has a higher frequency and a higher pitch than a deep voice. Quality: The unique characteristics of a sound that distinguish it from other sounds, such as the timbre or tone colour.

stem: The mass of a copper wire of resistance R1 and length l1 is four times the mass of another copper wire of length l2 and resistance R2. If R1 = R2, which one of the following is correct ?
solution: Let’s denote the mass, length, and cross-sectional area of the first wire as m1, l1, and A1, respectively. Similarly, for the second wire, we have m2, l2, and A2. Given: m1 = 4 × m2 R1 = R2 We know that the resistance of a wire is given by: R = rL A Where: r is the resistivity of the material (constant for copper) L is the length of the wire A is the cross-sectional area Since R1 = R2, we can write: ρ ρ L A L A 1 1 2 2 = ⇒ L A L A 1 1 = We also know that the mass of a wire is given by: m = rAL So, for the two wires: m1 = rA1L1 m2 = rA2L2 Given m1 = 4 × m2, we can write: rA1L1 = 4 × rA2L2 Dividing the two equations: L A L A 1 1 2 2 4 = × But we already know that L A L A 1 1 2 2 = . Therefore, the only way to satisfy this equation is if: L1 = 4 × L2
reviewNote: [RESOLVED — a second, independent blind derivation reached the printed key (C) without seeing it or the earlier objection, so the key stands. Basis: Both wires are copper, so density \(d\) and resistivity \(\rho\) are common to them. Writing \(S\) for the cross-section, mass is \(m = dSl\) and resistance is \(R = \rho l/S\), so \(S = \rho l/R\) and hence \(m = d\rho l^2/R\). With \(R_1 = R_2\) the mass is proportional to the square of the length, so \(m_1 = 4m_2\) gives \(l_1^2 = 4l_2^2\) and \(l_1 = 2l_2\). Checked for consistency: doubling the length at fixed resistance requires the area to double as well, so the volume and therefore the mass go up by a factor of four, as stated.]

subject: Physics
stem: Why does one experience a strong shock when one accidentally touches a live wire of say, 220 V?
optA: The resistance of human body is very low.
optB: The resistance of human body is very high.
optC: The human body is sensitive to even feeble currents.

solution: A person experiences a strong shock when they touch a live wire because the human body is sensitive to even feeble currents, and the live wire has a high potential: When a person touches a live wire, an electric current flows through their body. This current interferes with the electrical nerve process that controls the heartbeat, which causes a strong shock. Depending on the severity and length of the shock, injuries can include burns to the skin.

optD: depends upon the ratio of their frequencies.
solution: The velocity of both X-rays and gamma rays in a vacuum is the same because they are both forms of electromagnetic radiation. All electromagnetic waves travel at the speed of light in a vacuum, which is approximately 3 × 108 m/s. Their speed does not depend on their frequencies or wavelengths.

subject: Physics
stem: A stable nucleus ( light with A<10) has
optA: exactly the same number of neutrons and protons
solution: For light elements with a mass number A < 10, the most stable nuclei typically have an equal number of protons and neutrons. For example, deuterium (²H) is the most stable isotope of hydrogen with one proton and one neutron, while helium-4 (4He) has two protons and two neutrons. In heavier elements, the number of neutrons generally exceeds the number of protons to maintain nuclear stability. However, for light elements (A < 10), the nuclei are most stable when the number of protons and neutrons is balanced.

subject: Physics
stem: The penetrating power of X-rays can be increased by
optA: increasing the current in the filament.
optB: decreasing the potential difference between the cathode and the anode.
optC: decreasing the current in the filament.
optD: increasing the potential difference between the cathode and the anode.
solution: When we increase the potential difference between anode and cathode, then the energy of the striking electrons increases. Due to this, high energy electrons falling on the metal surface, the X-rays produced get more energy. The penetrating power of X-rays increases when we increase the energy of X-rays.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which one among the following is not a mixture?
solution: Graphite is not a mixture, while glass, brass and steel are Graphite: A pure, natural form of crystalline carbon that is found in metamorphic and igneous rocks. It is made up of only carbon atoms, so it is an element, not a mixture. Glass: A transparent, non-crystalline solid made by heating a mixture of raw materials like sand and soda ash until it forms a viscous state. Brass: An alloy made up of copper and zinc, so it is a mixture. Steel: An alloy made up of iron, carbon and other elements, so it is a mixture.

stem: Which one among the following statements is not correct about graphite?

solution: The statement that graphite is the higher grade of coal is not correct. Graphite is a pure form of carbon, while coal is a sedimentary rock made up of fossilised plant matter.

stem: Which one among the following metals is more reactive than hydrogen?
solution: Tin is more reactive than hydrogen, meaning it can displace hydrogen from acids in a similar manner to more reactive metals. In contrast, mercury, copper and silver are less reactive than hydrogen. They do not readily react with acids to produce hydrogen gas, which is why they are not considered more reactive than hydrogen.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which one of the following is a transition metal?
solution: Manganese (Mn) is a transition metal, while aluminium (Al), magnesium (Mg) and calcium (Ca) are not- Manganese: A transition metal with partially filled d-orbitals, located in period 4 and group 7 of the periodic table. Transition metals are useful in many applications, including catalysis, electronics and medicine. Aluminium: A post-transition metal in the boron group, with filled s and p orbitals. Magnesium: A non-transition metal with filled s orbitals, located in group 2 of the periodic table. Calcium: A non-transition metal with filled s orbitals, located in group 2 of the periodic table.

subject: Chemistry
stem: What is the reason for white cement to be white?
solution: The reason for the whiteness of white cement is the absence of iron oxide. Iron oxide (Fe2O3) is an important constituent of cement. It imparts a greyish colour of cement. While manufacturing white cement, the percentage of iron oxide is minimised to a great extent.

subject: Biology
stem: Which one of the following contains powerful oxidative enzymes and help in removing toxic substances from cells?
solution: Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles that contain hydrolytic enzymes that can break down old cell parts, viruses, bacteria and foreign bodies. They are also known as “suicidal bags” because they can digest the entire cell if it is damaged beyond repair. When a cell is about to die, the lysosome bursts open and begins to eat away the cell organelles.

subject: Biology
stem: Which one of the following is not a genetic disorder?
solution: Xerophthalmia: A severe drying of the eye surface caused by a malfunction of the tear glands. It’s most commonly caused by decreased intake or absorption of vitamin A. Some examples of genetic disorders include: Haemophilia: An X-linked recessive genetic disorder that occurs due to deficiency of clotting factors in the blood. Sickle cell anaemia: An autosomal recessive genetic disorder in which red blood cells become sickle- shaped. Colour blindness: A sex-linked inherited disorder.
